1.why: owner() binds every MFA endpoint to session.userId and loads only that account, so settings are always owner-scoped.

2.why: TOTP is verified against the account’s own encrypted secret and recovery codes against that account’s hashes, so one user’s code does not authenticate another.

3.why: Enabling MFA updates only the current session’s stage and account flags; no other sessions for the user are invalidated.

4.why: mfaSecretEncrypted uses AES-GCM encrypt(); backup codes are stored as PBKDF2 hashes with per-code salts.

5.why: tokens, OTP digits, base32 secrets, and recovery codes all come from crypto.getRandomValues via bytes()/randomChars().

6.why: Session is only in an HttpOnly Secure cookie; CSRF/secret/codes live in JS memory, not localStorage/sessionStorage or non-HttpOnly cookies.

7.why: Server validates email, phone, OTP, recovery, and manual secret with dedicated validators before use.

8.why: UI builds DOM with textContent/createElement; API responses are JSON; no unencoded reflection of user input into HTML.

9.why: No redirect responses exist at all, so open redirects are absent though no explicit allow-list is implemented.

10.why: headers() sets CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options DENY and frame-ancestors 'none'.

11.why: sessionCookie() sets HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict on Host-mfa_session.

12.why: Errors are generic and tokens are not in URLs/logs, but testMode can return testingCode and the client console.logs recovery/OTP material.

13.why: Identity OTPs are single-use with codeMs expiry; TOTP rejects reused counters; recovery codes are removed after successful use.

14.why: identity/otp/recovery failures lock out after 5 tries (lockMs) and identity requests are throttled.

15.why: Sign-in deletes the old session and issues a new token; idle/absolute timeouts apply; logout sets invalidated and clears the cookie.
